title: Attachment Adventure
welcome_lead: Why do babies cling to their carers? 🤱
meta_desc: Development & Attachment Adventure 2 — KS3 Psychology on Bowlby's attachment theory.
final_note: You met Bowlby's attachment theory and how secure bonds help us grow.

concepts.def: Strong emotional bond with a carer
The person who looks after a child

walkthroughs.body_html:
John Bowlby said babies form a strong bond — attachment — with a main carer in their first year.

This helps them feel safe and explore the world.

Secure attachment — child trusts the carer, plays happily, copes with brief partings.

Insecure attachment — child is anxious, clingy or distant.

Securely attached children often grow up better at:

  • Making friends.
  • Coping with stress.
  • Building healthy adult relationships.

It's not destiny — but it's a strong start. ❤️

mcqs.q: In Pavlov's experiment, what is the conditioned response?
options: Salivation to the bell alone, after pairing with food.
The dog ringing the bell itself.
Cries continuously and cannot be comforted.
Salivation to the food (which is automatic).

mcqs.q: How does a securely attached infant respond to reunion with the caregiver?
options: Seeks comfort and is easily soothed, then returns to play.
Shows no distress and ignores the caregiver.
Cries continuously and cannot be comforted.
The dog ringing the bell itself.
